name: rice
description: Rice is a major staple crop that performs well in warm, humid conditions. Suitable soil and water-management requirements vary with cultivar and production system. Clayey or alluvial soils can be suitable where water retention, permeability and drainage are appropriate.
soil_characteristics: Clayey or alluvial soils with suitable water-retention and permeability. Flooded transplanted paddy benefits from a hardpan that restricts deep percolation. Direct-seeded and aerobic rice systems suit well-structured, permeable soils.
climate_requirements: Warm, humid conditions with temperatures typically in the 22°C–27°C range during active growth. Water availability and management must align with the chosen production system (flooded, DSR, AWD, or aerobic). Avoid temperatures above 35°C at anthesis.
fertilizer_tips: Apply N, P and K according to soil-test results, crop establishment method, cultivar and local extension recommendations (e.g. ICAR/SAU guidelines). Nitrogen is commonly applied in split doses around establishment, tillering and panicle initiation. Apply zinc sulphate only where zinc deficiency or deficiency risk is established by soil or tissue testing.
crop_notes: Water and nutrient management strategy is highly dependent on the production system selected (flooded transplanted, DSR, AWD, or aerobic rice). Consult regional ICAR/KVK extension guidance before prescribing any specific nutrient rates.

name: maize
description: Maize is a high-yielding cereal grain cultivated for human consumption, livestock feed, and industrial starch. It typically performs well in well-drained, fertile loamy soils under abundant sunshine and warm temperatures.
soil_characteristics: Well-drained loamy or sandy-loam soils with good aeration. Tolerates a range of soil types but performs poorly in waterlogged or compacted soils.
climate_requirements: Warm seasons with moderate to abundant sunshine. Susceptible to frost. Water stress during silking and grain fill significantly reduces yield.
fertilizer_tips: Apply phosphorus and potassium based on certified soil test. Split nitrogen applications are commonly used across establishment, knee-high stage, and pre-tassel. Rates depend on yield target, soil OM, and previous crop history.
crop_notes: Widely grown in both Kharif (summer) and Rabi (winter) seasons in India. Cultivar selection significantly affects nutrient demand and harvest duration.

name: chickpea
description: Chickpea is a cool-season legume that fixes atmospheric nitrogen. It typically performs in semi-arid environments with deep, well-aerated soils and low to moderate moisture.
ideal_n_range: 15–45 kg/ha (indicative; N fixation reduces synthetic N requirement)
soil_characteristics: Deep, well-aerated sandy-loam to loam soils. Poor drainage and waterlogging are detrimental. Prefers neutral to slightly alkaline pH.
climate_requirements: Cool, dry weather during grain fill and maturity. Warm humid conditions at flowering increase disease risk (Botrytis grey mould).
fertilizer_tips: Inoculate seeds with Rhizobium before sowing where rhizobial populations are low. Apply starter phosphorus and sulfur based on soil test. Excessive nitrogen suppresses nodulation.
crop_notes: Biological nitrogen fixation can contribute 60–170 kg N/ha under favourable conditions, reducing the need for synthetic nitrogen. Actual contribution depends on cultivar, soil rhizobial population, and growing conditions.

name: kidneybeans
description: Kidney beans are nutritious pulse legumes that typically perform well at moderate temperatures in loose, organic-rich, well-drained soils. They are sensitive to waterlogging.
soil_characteristics: Loose, organic-rich, well-drained loamy soils. Sensitive to saline conditions and waterlogging.
climate_requirements: Cool to moderate temperatures. High temperatures during flowering may reduce pod set. Avoid frost exposure.
fertilizer_tips: Apply well-decomposed organic matter at land preparation. Basal phosphorus supports root and pod development. Consult soil test before applying any synthetic nutrient.
crop_notes: Commonly grown as a Rabi (cool-season) crop in hilly and highland regions of India.

name: pigeonpeas
description: Pigeon peas are deep-rooted, drought-tolerant legumes widely grown in tropical and subtropical drylands. They fix nitrogen and tolerate variable rainfall patterns.
harvest_duration: 150 – 200 days (cultivar dependent; short- to long-duration varieties)
soil_characteristics: Well-drained loam to sandy-loam soils. Deep taproots allow access to sub-soil moisture. Waterlogging is damaging.
climate_requirements: Warm tropical to subtropical conditions. Short-day photoperiod sensitivity affects flowering in some cultivars. Drought-tolerant once established.
fertilizer_tips: Apply a starter dose of nitrogen and phosphorus based on soil test. Rhizobium inoculation is beneficial in fields with low rhizobial populations. Excessive nitrogen suppresses nodulation.
crop_notes: One of the most important Kharif pulse crops in India. Duration ranges from 120 days (early/medium) to 270+ days (late-maturing varieties).

name: mothbeans
description: Moth bean is among the most drought-hardy legumes, forming a dense vegetative cover that conserves soil moisture and prevents erosion in arid sandy belts.
soil_characteristics: Sandy to sandy-loam soils; very drought-tolerant. Poor performance in waterlogged soils.
climate_requirements: Hot, arid to semi-arid conditions. One of the few legumes suited to very low rainfall environments.
fertilizer_tips: Very low synthetic nutrient demand due to nitrogen fixation and adaptation to poor soils. Apply a minimal starter phosphorus dose based on soil test only if soil P is confirmed low.
crop_notes: Primarily cultivated in the arid zones of Rajasthan, Gujarat, and Maharashtra. Significant contributor to smallholder food security under very low rainfall.

name: mungbean
description: Mung bean is a quick-maturing, highly digestible pulse well-suited to short-duration crop rotations in warm weather with loamy, well-drained soils.
soil_characteristics: Warm, loamy, well-drained soils. Sensitive to waterlogging. Short duration makes it suitable as a relay or catch crop.
climate_requirements: Warm temperatures; sensitive to frost. Suitable for spring-summer and Kharif seasons.
fertilizer_tips: Rhizobium and phosphorus-solubilising bacteria seed treatment is beneficial. Apply basal phosphorus according to soil test. Foliar phosphorus sprays at flowering may support pod formation in low-P soils.
crop_notes: Widely grown as a short-duration crop after wheat or as a Kharif season crop. Pods mature non-uniformly; staggered harvesting or once-over harvesting depending on crop type.

name: blackgram
description: Black gram is an important protein-rich legume that improves soil fertility through biological nitrogen fixation. It favours warm conditions and moisture-retentive loamy soils.
soil_characteristics: Loamy, moisture-retentive soils with good drainage. Tolerates a range of soil types but prefers neutral to mildly alkaline pH.
climate_requirements: Warm humid conditions during vegetative stage. Cool and dry weather at maturity helps pod quality.
fertilizer_tips: Apply balanced phosphorus based on soil test. Potassium application may be considered on confirmed low-K soils. Rhizobium inoculation supports nitrogen fixation.
crop_notes: Grown in both Kharif and Rabi seasons. Key ingredient in South Asian cuisine. Pod shattering at maturity may require careful harvest timing.

name: lentil
description: Lentil is a resilient cool-season legume grown in winter (Rabi) season. It adapts to varying soil types from light sandy loams to alluvial soils and provides nutrient-rich edible seeds.
soil_characteristics: Light sandy loam to alluvial soils. Well-drained, neutral to slightly alkaline soils are generally suitable.
climate_requirements: Cool dry growing season. Frost-tolerant to a degree. High temperatures during grain fill reduce seed quality.
fertilizer_tips: Apply starter nitrogen (limited) and phosphorus as basal placement below the seed based on soil test. Rhizobium inoculation is beneficial. Avoid excessive irrigation during vegetative growth.
crop_notes: An important Rabi pulse in the Indo-Gangetic plains. Soil-test-based fertilisation is strongly recommended given the variability in soil P and K across different regions.

name: pomegranate
description: Pomegranate is a drought-tolerant fruit crop well-suited to dry, semi-arid regions with deep loamy soils and hot summers. It is commercially important in Maharashtra, Karnataka, and Gujarat.
soil_characteristics: Deep loamy soils. Tolerates a range of soil types including slightly saline. Waterlogging is damaging.
climate_requirements: Hot dry summers and mild winters. A dry period preceding harvest improves fruit quality. High humidity at harvest increases disease risk.
fertilizer_tips: Apply well-rotted organic compost annually. Mineral nutrient applications should be based on leaf tissue analysis and soil test. Potassium and calcium are particularly important for fruit quality.
crop_notes: Perennial crop; fertiliser requirements change with tree age and bearing status. Consult SAU/ICAR regional orchard management recommendations.

name: banana
description: Banana is a fast-growing tropical fruit requiring warm temperatures, high humidity, and deep, humus-rich alluvial soils with continuous moisture and excellent drainage.
ideal_n_range: 80–200 g/plant/year (indicative; highly cultivar and yield dependent)
harvest_duration: 9 – 12 months from planting (cultivar and temperature dependent)
soil_characteristics: Deep, well-drained alluvial or loamy soils high in organic matter. Sensitive to waterlogging and strong winds.
climate_requirements: Tropical, warm and humid year-round. Susceptible to frost and cold winds. Requires wind shelter in exposed sites.
fertilizer_tips: Banana is a heavy potassium feeder. Apply N, P and K in multiple splits across the crop cycle based on tissue analysis and soil test. Rates depend strongly on target yield, cultivar, and soil type.
crop_notes: Nutrient requirements are typically expressed per plant per year. Consult ICAR/NHB or SAU recommendations specific to cultivar (e.g. Grand Naine, Nendran, Robusta) and agro-climatic zone.

name: mango
description: Mango is a major tropical fruit crop requiring warm sunny climates and well-drained deep loamy soils. A distinct dry period preceding flowering promotes profuse bloom induction.
ideal_n_range: Varies by tree age and bearing; expressed per tree/year (indicative)
ideal_p_range: Varies by tree age; based on soil test and leaf analysis (indicative)
ideal_k_range: Varies by tree age; potassium-responsive crop (indicative)
water_requirement: ~500 – 1,500 mm/year (indicative; supplemental irrigation at critical stages)
soil_characteristics: Deep, well-drained loamy soils. Tolerates a range of soil types but performs poorly in waterlogged or very heavy clay soils.
climate_requirements: Warm tropical conditions with a dry period (ideally 2–3 months) preceding flowering to ensure floral bud differentiation. Frost-sensitive.
fertilizer_tips: Apply farmyard manure and mineral fertilisers post-monsoon based on soil test and leaf tissue analysis. Withhold irrigation for 6–8 weeks before flowering to promote floral bud differentiation. Exact rates depend on tree age, cultivar, and yield target.
crop_notes: Perennial fruit tree. Fertiliser requirements change with tree age (young, pre-bearing, bearing). Consult NHB/ICAR mango production guidelines for region-specific recommendations.

name: grapes
description: Grapes are high-value commercial fruits grown on trellised vines in warm, dry climates. They typically require porous, gravelly or sandy loam soils and sunny, low-humidity ripening conditions.
ideal_n_range: 15–50 kg/ha (indicative; varies by training system and yield target)
soil_characteristics: Porous, well-drained gravelly, sandy or loamy soils. Good drainage is essential; waterlogging causes root disease.
climate_requirements: Warm sunny growing season with low humidity during ripening. Requires a cool dormancy period for bud break. Rain at harvest increases disease pressure.
fertilizer_tips: Potassium is particularly important for berry sugar content and skin quality. Apply nitrogen conservatively; excess delays ripening. Base all nutrient applications on petiole/leaf tissue analysis and soil test.
crop_notes: Nutrient management varies significantly by training system (VSP, Y-trellis, bower), cultivar, and target end use (table, raisin, wine). Consult NRCP/ICAR Pune or NHB guidelines.

name: watermelon
description: Watermelon is a warm-season vining fruit demanding prolonged sunshine, high temperatures, and well-drained sandy or sandy-loam soils.
soil_characteristics: Well-drained sandy or sandy-loam soils. Sensitive to waterlogging.
climate_requirements: Long warm sunny season. Sensitive to frost. Low humidity at ripening reduces disease pressure.
fertilizer_tips: Apply nitrogen in split doses. Restrict excess nitrogen and reduce irrigation during fruit ripening to improve sugar content. Potassium supports fruit quality. Base all rates on soil test.
crop_notes: Often grown on river-bed soils in Zaid season. Grafting onto bottle-gourd or bitter-gourd rootstocks is practiced to manage soil-borne diseases.

name: muskmelon
description: Muskmelon thrives in hot, arid to semi-arid climates with sandy loam soils. It requires clear sunny days and low ambient humidity to develop its characteristic sweet aroma.
soil_characteristics: Sandy to sandy-loam soils with good drainage. Sensitive to waterlogging.
climate_requirements: Hot, low-humidity growing season. Overhead sprinkler irrigation should be avoided to reduce mildew risk. Dry conditions at ripening improve fruit aroma.
fertilizer_tips: Apply balanced NPK based on soil test at planting. Drip fertigation is common for commercial production. Cease irrigation 7–10 days before harvest to concentrate sugars. Consult extension recommendations for split schedules.
crop_notes: Often grown in Zaid season on riverbed or upland sandy soils. Cultivar selection significantly affects fruit quality and market preference.

name: apple
description: Apples typically perform in temperate highland environments with cool winters and warm summers. They require deep, well-drained loamy soils and sufficient winter chilling for bud-break and uniform flowering.
ideal_n_range: Based on annual shoot growth and mid-season leaf tissue N (target ~2.0–2.4% dry wt); highly cultivar dependent
ideal_p_range: Based on certified soil test and leaf tissue analysis (indicative)
ideal_k_range: Based on certified soil test and leaf tissue analysis (indicative)
harvest_duration: Cultivar dependent (~120 – 180 days from full bloom)
soil_characteristics: Deep, well-drained loamy soils with adequate organic matter. At least 75–100 cm of permeable rooting depth required. Poor subsoil drainage is a significant constraint.
climate_requirements: Temperate highland conditions. Requires sufficient winter chilling hours (cultivar-specific: low-chill cultivars 250–400 hours; standard commercial cultivars 800–1,100+ hours below 7.2°C). Late frost at bloom is a major yield risk.
fertilizer_tips: Base soil fertility programmes on a calibrated pre-planting soil test and midsummer leaf tissue analysis. Do not prescribe fixed kg/ha rates without these inputs. Consult regional SAU or ICAR/CITH (Himachal Pradesh) orchard nutrition guidelines.
crop_notes: Perennial fruit tree. Nutrient requirements change with tree age, bearing status, and rootstock. Winter chilling requirement is the primary site-selection criterion — verify with local agro-meteorological data before planting.

name: orange
description: Oranges are a premier citrus fruit favouring subtropical conditions with good sunshine and well-drained, light sandy or alluvial loams free from subsoil hardpans.
ideal_n_range: Expressed per tree/year; varies with tree age and cultivar (indicative)
ideal_p_range: Expressed per tree/year; based on soil test and leaf analysis (indicative)
water_requirement: ~900 – 1,500 mm/year (indicative; supplemental irrigation at critical stages)
harvest_duration: 8 – 12 months from flowering (cultivar and climate dependent)
soil_characteristics: Light sandy to alluvial loam soils, free of sub-soil hardpan. Good internal drainage is essential to prevent root diseases.
climate_requirements: Subtropical conditions with seasonal temperature variation to induce flowering. High humidity at maturity can reduce fruit quality and increase post-harvest disease.
fertilizer_tips: Apply nitrogen in multiple splits coinciding with growth flushes. Micronutrient deficiencies (zinc, iron, manganese) are common in citrus — diagnose by leaf symptom and tissue test before applying foliar sprays. Consult NHB/ICAR citrus nutrition recommendations.
crop_notes: Widely grown in Nagpur, Vidarbha, Coorg, Punjab, and Rajasthan. Fertiliser expression in grams per tree per year (GPT) is conventional for citrus. Consult region-specific SAU or NHB guidelines.

name: papaya
description: Papaya is a fast-producing tropical fruit tree that performs in warm, well-aerated sandy loam soils. It is extremely sensitive to waterlogging and frost.
ideal_n_range: Expressed per plant/year; varies with cultivar and target yield (indicative)
ideal_p_range: Expressed per plant/year; based on soil test (indicative)
soil_characteristics: Well-aerated sandy loam soils with excellent drainage. Waterlogging — even brief — causes collar rot and plant death.
climate_requirements: Warm tropical conditions year-round. Frost-sensitive. High humidity combined with poor drainage increases Phytophthora collar rot risk.
fertilizer_tips: Apply NPK in monthly splits based on plant age and target yield. Rates should be calibrated from certified soil test and local extension guidance. Organic mulch around the root zone helps retain moisture and add OM.
crop_notes: TNAU, ICAR-NRCP and NHB provide region-specific papaya nutrition schedules. Ring drainage is essential to protect crown roots in high-rainfall areas.

name: coconut
description: Coconut palm is a classic tropical plantation crop flourishing in coastal alluvial and sandy soils with steady year-round humidity, sunlight, and adequate soil aeration.
ideal_n_range: Expressed per palm/year; varies with age, yield, and soil type (indicative)
ideal_p_range: Expressed per palm/year; phosphorus-responsive on low-P soils (indicative)
ideal_k_range: Expressed per palm/year; potassium is the most important macronutrient for coconut (indicative)
water_requirement: ~1,500 – 2,500 mm/year (indicative; supplemental drip irrigation beneficial in drier periods)
harvest_duration: Continuous harvest cycle; nuts mature ~12 months after pollination
soil_characteristics: Sandy to alluvial coastal soils with good internal drainage. Saline-tolerant to a degree. Waterlogging is damaging to root systems.
climate_requirements: Warm, humid tropical coastal conditions with year-round sunshine. Wind exposure is a risk factor requiring windbreak consideration in some sites.
fertilizer_tips: Potassium is the critical nutrient for coconut. Apply NPK and magnesium in 2 seasonal doses (pre-monsoon and post-monsoon) based on certified soil and leaf tissue analysis. Salt (NaCl) applications may be beneficial in coastal areas where sodium is deficient.
crop_notes: CPCRI (Central Plantation Crops Research Institute) and KAU provide region-specific coconut nutrition schedules. Nutrient expression is per palm per year. Consult age-of-palm-specific recommendations.

name: cotton
description: Cotton is a major commercial fibre crop best adapted to deep black soils (Vertisols/regur) with strong moisture retention, warm sunny days, and dry weather during boll opening.
ideal_n_range: 80–150 kg/ha (indicative; Bt hybrid cotton has different N response curves)
soil_characteristics: Deep black cotton soils (Vertisols) are traditionally preferred for their high water-holding capacity. Alluvial and loamy soils are also suitable with appropriate management.
climate_requirements: Warm sunny Kharif season with dry weather during boll development and opening. Cloudy weather during boll maturation significantly reduces lint quality. Temperature above 38°C at flowering reduces boll retention.
fertilizer_tips: Apply phosphorus and potassium according to soil test. Split nitrogen at squaring, first flowering, and peak boll development stages. Bt hybrid varieties may have different nitrogen response profiles compared to non-Bt varieties. Consult CICR/ICAR or SAU recommendations.
crop_notes: Bt hybrid cotton dominates commercial cultivation in India. Fertiliser response varies significantly between Bt and non-Bt varieties. Magnesium deficiency (leaf reddening) is common on sandy or depleted soils.

name: jute
description: Jute is a premier bast fibre crop cultivated in warm, humid deltaic regions with heavy monsoons. It typically performs in alluvial flood plains with periodic silt replenishment.
soil_characteristics: Alluvial, silty-loam or loamy soils in riverine plains. Periodic silt deposition replenishes nutrients naturally in flood-prone regions.
climate_requirements: Hot, humid tropical conditions with heavy monsoon rainfall. Short-day plant — day length affects maturity timing.
fertilizer_tips: Apply balanced NPK at sowing based on soil test. Top-dress urea at 4–6 weeks coinciding with weeding. Adequate potassium improves fibre tensile strength. Rates should be confirmed from regional NIRJAFT/ICAR jute extension recommendations.
crop_notes: Primarily cultivated in West Bengal, Assam, Bihar, and Odisha. Retting method (water retting vs. ribbon retting) affects fibre quality. NIRJAFT recommendations are the primary reference for jute agronomy.

name: coffee
description: Coffee is an evergreen shade-grown plantation crop thriving on tropical highland hillslopes with permeable, fertile soils high in organic matter. Arabica and Robusta have different climatic requirements.
ideal_n_range: Varies by species and tree age; expressed per plant or per ha (indicative)
ideal_p_range: Varies by species and soil type; based on soil test (indicative)
ideal_k_range: Potassium-responsive; important for bean quality and yield (indicative)
harvest_duration: 8 – 10 months from flowering to berry ripeness (species and altitude dependent)
soil_characteristics: Permeable, fertile volcanic or forest loams high in organic matter. Good internal drainage is essential. Shade tree management is integral to production system.
climate_requirements: Tropical highland conditions. Arabica requires cooler temperatures (1,000–1,800 m altitude); Robusta is more heat-tolerant. Seasonal rainfall distribution affects flowering uniformity.
fertilizer_tips: Apply NPK in split doses coinciding with blossom showers and post-monsoon berry swelling. Organic mulch helps maintain soil moisture and adds OM. Rates depend on species, yield target, soil test, and estate elevation. Consult Coffee Board of India recommendations.
crop_notes: The Coffee Board of India publishes species- and region-specific nutrient management schedules. Shade management significantly affects microclimate and disease pressure. Arabica and Robusta have markedly different agronomic profiles.
